name: Stachys
overview: Stachys is a male figure mentioned in the New Testament, specifically noted for being beloved by the Apostle Paul. While there is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details, his close relationship with Paul highlights his significance within the early Christian community.
namesAndTitles: The name Stachys appears only once in Scripture, in Romans 16:9, with no specific meaning provided. It is a proper name of Greek origin and does not carry a divine attribution in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Stachys beyond his designation as beloved by Paul. There are no other relational details given in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Stachys is significant in the biblical narrative primarily because of his close association with the Apostle Paul, indicating a trusted and valued member of the early church. His mention in Romans 16:9 among Paul's greetings suggests he played a meaningful role in supporting the ministry and the spread of the Gospel during the formative years of the Christian movement.
